display.purpose: Hero name headline only (rendered larger than the base token, clamp(72px, 13vw, 208px), for the full-bleed hero); italic gradient-fill variant marks the accent word.

headline.purpose: Section titles — Services, Shorts, Feed, Contact all resolve to this one shared value.

title.purpose: Service card titles, paired with an italic numeral and a tag pill.

body.purpose: Hero tagline, Shorts body, Contact body, service descriptions. Max ~58ch line length.

label.purpose: Language toggle, tag pills, duration/price micro-labels, footer credit line. Always uppercase, bold, tracked.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Service cards on hover (shadow-only transition; no translateY on the card in the current implementation).

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Slow, calm ease-out for all scroll-triggered reveals (0.8-1.4s).

motion.name: ease-transition
motion.purpose: Same curve for hover/UI transitions (250ms), consistent editorial feel.

components.name: Button (solid-dark)
components.description: Dark pill CTA on light backgrounds, e.g. the Feed "Follow on Instagram" link.
components.css: .ds-btn-solid-dark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: #3b2e26; color: #f6efe4; padding: 16px 26px; border-radius: 999px; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); } .ds-btn-solid-dark:hover { opacity: 0.88; } .ds-btn-solid-dark:active { opacity: 0.75; } .ds-btn-solid-dark:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c98e84; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Button (solid-accent)
components.description: Terracotta pill CTA, the highest-intent action on the page (Hero and Contact Telegram buttons). Uses the darkened accent-text token, not the raw accent, so white text stays WCAG AA (5.57:1 vs 2.73:1). Includes a subtle tap pulse-ring, hidden under prefers-reduced-motion.
components.css: .ds-btn-solid-accent { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: #9a5548; color: #ffffff; padding: 16px 26px; border-radius: 999px; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); } .ds-btn-solid-accent:hover { opacity: 0.88; } .ds-btn-solid-accent:active { opacity: 0.75; } .ds-btn-solid-accent:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b2e26; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tag / Chip
components.description: Small uppercase pill for service tags on ServiceCard ("online", "video", "Tallinn").
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #e4cfc6; color: #7a4e45; border-radius: 999px; padding: 7px 16px; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Service Card
components.description: Interactive link card: thumbnail, title/tag/description, price/CTA. The site's signature component, rendered in two variants — a horizontally pinned-scroll 'panel' (default) and a vertically stacked row (reduced-motion fallback). CTA links carry a pre-filled, service-specific Telegram message.
components.html:
Account Review

Profile audit, personality unpacking and positioning.

150 €
components.css: .ds-service-card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 128px 1fr auto; gap: 32px; align-items: center; background: #f8f2e8; border-radius: 24px; padding: 22px; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; box-shadow: 0 2px 0 rgba(59, 46, 38, 0.04); transition: box-shadow 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); } .ds-service-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 22px 44px rgba(59, 46, 38, 0.12); } .ds-service-card__thumb { aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; border-radius: 18px; background: #e2d4c5; } .ds-service-card__title { font-family: 'Playfair Display', serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 30px; margin: 0 0 8px; color: #3b2e26; } .ds-service-card__desc { font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #6b5a4e; margin: 0; } .ds-service-card__price { font-family: 'Playfair Display', serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 30px; color: #3b2e26; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Language Toggle
components.description: The only persistent control in the chrome-free header. A pill-shaped segmented control showing both en/ru codes side by side; the active locale sits on an animated accent pill with white text.
components.css: .ds-lang-toggle { display: inline-flex; gap: 2px; background: #e4cfc6; border-radius: 999px; padding: 4px; } .ds-lang-toggle__option { border-radius: 999px; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #7a4e45; opacity: 0.55; transition: opacity 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1), background 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); } .ds-lang-toggle__option--active { background: #9a5548; color: #ffffff; opacity: 1; }

components.name: Section Kicker
components.description: Small uppercase tracked label used sparingly — currently only on Contact's navigational label above the contact-links list. Not repeated as decorative scaffolding on every section.
components.css: .ds-kicker { font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.22em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #c98e84; margin-bottom: 16px; }

narrative.overview: The site reads as a real person's creative workspace, not a productized funnel: soft cream walls, terracotta accents, natural light. Every surface is warm and matte — no glass, no corporate blue. The pacing is slow and editorial, like flipping through a mentor's own portfolio rather than scrolling a SaaS pricing page. Playfair Display carries the personality but only in isolated accent moments — the accent word in the hero H1, service numerals — never a whole heading or wordmark; Nunito Sans stays quiet and does the informational work. Every section title resolves to one shared headline size rather than five ad hoc values, and the small uppercase kicker label appears only where it carries real information (Contact's navigational label), not as decorative scaffolding repeated on every section. The shipped page is deliberately hero-first and lean: Header, Hero, Services, Shorts, Feed, Contact — no persistent navigation, no header CTA, and no dedicated Mission or About section. The hero portrait and copy voice alone carry "this is a real person," and every scroll depth funnels toward the single Contact panel at the bottom. This system explicitly rejects generic SaaS/agency consultant templates — corporate blue gradients, stock-photo grids, hero-metric stat rows, gradient-text headlines — and loud influencer/hustle-culture aesthetics — neon accents, countdown urgency, aggressive upsell language. The brand is one real person's warm, editorial space.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color (#c98e84, dusty terracotta, with a darkened #9a5548 text-safe variant) used sparingly — tags, CTAs, the footer credit link, selection color
Fully rounded pill buttons and generously rounded cards (18–28px), never sharp corners
Playfair Display italic reserved for isolated accent moments (the Hero accent word, service numerals) — never a whole heading or wordmark
A single shared headline size across all section titles, not five ad hoc values
No section kickers except Contact's literal navigational label — not repeated as decorative scaffolding on every section
Flat, matte surfaces layered by warmth (parchment → paper → cream → ink), no shadows for depth except soft ambient lift on hover
Slow reveals (0.8–1.4s) — nothing snaps or bounces
A bare, chrome-free header: just a language toggle, no logo, no nav, no persistent CTA

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Only #c98e84 / #9a5548 (dusty terracotta and its text-safe darkened variant) carry color intent across the whole site. Every other value is a neutral tinted from the ink-to-parchment ramp. If a second saturated color is needed, tint it from the existing ramp rather than introducing a new hue. Known exception: GradientText.tsx on the Hero's "Kupczyk" word animates a background-clip gradient — a live, isolated departure from this rule, not a pattern to repeat.

rules.name: The Italic Warmth Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display italic is reserved for moments of personality: the accent word in the Hero H1, service numerals. Never used for body copy, functional UI text, or an entire wordmark — it marks emotional beats only.

rules.name: The One Headline Rule
rules.body: Every section title (h2) resolves to the same --text-headline value. A section that wants to feel bigger earns it through layout (width, surrounding whitespace, color contrast), not through a private font-size. The Hero h1 is exempt — it uses the larger Display tier by design.

rules.name: The Diffuse-Only Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in the system uses the ink color at low opacity (4–12%) with a large blur radius. No hard-edged or dark shadows anywhere — the warmth of the palette carries into elevation too.

dos: Do keep the accent color (#c98e84 / #9a5548) to a single deliberate role per section — a CTA, a tag, or the footer credit link, never more than one saturated moment per screenful.
Do use full pill radius (999px) on every button, no exceptions.
Do reserve Playfair Display italic for personality beats (the Hero accent word, service numerals), never for body copy, UI labels, or an entire wordmark.
Do keep shadows diffuse and ink-tinted (4–12% opacity, large blur) — never a hard, dark drop shadow.
Do pace reveals slowly (0.8–1.4s, cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)) — this is an editorial, unhurried brand, not a SaaS product.
Do use --color-accent-text (#9a5548), never the raw --color-accent, wherever white text sits on the accent fill — the raw accent fails WCAG AA at 2.73:1.
Do resolve every section headline to the single shared --text-headline value — a bigger-feeling section earns it through layout, not a private font-size.
Do treat the header as intentionally minimal — a new feature should not assume a logo, nav links, or a persistent header CTA exist to hook into.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for any new scroll-driven or transform-heavy interaction, following the stacked/panel pattern in Services.
donts: Don't introduce corporate blue gradients, stock-photo grids, hero-metric stat rows, or gradient-text headlines — the generic SaaS/agency consultant template this brand explicitly rejects (the existing GradientText on "Kupczyk" is a known, isolated exception, not license for a second instance).
Don't use neon accents, countdown urgency, or aggressive upsell language — the loud influencer/hustle-culture aesthetic this brand explicitly rejects.
Don't use sharp corners or hard shadows anywhere; every corner is rounded, every shadow is soft.
Don't add a second saturated hue. If more color is needed, tint further along the existing ink-to-parchment ramp.
Don't use top/left/width/height in any animation — transform and opacity only, per the site's hardware-acceleration rule.
Don't add a SectionKicker to a new section by reflex — it earns its place only when it carries real information, not as decorative section grammar.
Don't add new anchor links assuming a nav exists to house them — there is currently no in-page navigation, and the existing section ids are unlinked.
Don't ship a new scroll-hijacking or pinned-scroll interaction without a visible progress indicator and a viewport-based or reduced-motion opt-out.
